title: Banyan Insights - Scale Path and Contract Extension Sync
summary: Customer currently on hosted plan, projecting increased usage over next 6 months. Discussed options: step-up to Dedicated reserved capacity vs hybrid (hosted + dedicated burst), private VPC pilot in eu-central-1, target latency and throughput, pricing/commitment mechanics and security artifacts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send revised quote with 6-month ramp pricing, security packet, and schedule a 2-hour benchmark run with sample workload for week of May 26. Action owners assigned.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (CSM) — Maya Chen (CTO, Banyan), Jon Rivera (Head of ML Ops), Priya Nair (Procurement), Evan Liu (SRE)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into where Banyan is on usage and what you want from the extension.
[00:12] Maya (Banyan): Hi, Maya here. Thanks.
[00:14] Jon (Banyan): Jon here.
[00:16] Priya (Banyan): Priya.
[00:18] Evan (Banyan): Evan here.
[00:20] Alex: Great. Samir, do you want to kick off with a short status on our side?
[00:25] Samir (Redwood SE): Yeah sure. So my understanding from last time — Banyan is running in our hosted tier, roughly steady state about 5m tokens/day, peaks around 8m, and you're starting a marketing drive next quarter that we expect will push that up. Is that still accurate, Jon?
[00:40] Jon: Yeah, that's correct. The campaign in June could put us at about 20M tokens/day at peak weekends. Sorry — I know tokens are weird metric — that's roughly 2.5x current. Latency p95 target for user-facing is 300 milliseconds, ideally under 250 but we can accept up to 300.
[01:05] Samir: Got it. The two levers we typically discuss are: move to a Dedicated reserved pool to guarantee throughput, or remain hosted and purchase burst capacity + priority routing. Both have cost and operational tradeoffs.
[01:20] Maya: Right, we want to avoid user-visible slowdowns. Also data residency — EU customers need processing in Germany, so we want an eu-central-1 VPC/private pilot eventually.
[01:33] Alex: That makes sense. On residency — Redwood Private/VPC is the path; we can run a pilot with a private control plane and customer-managed VPC peering. That will bring in the security checklist items — SAML SSO, KMS integration for keys, audit logs, etc.
[01:50] Priya: For procurement, we also need SOC 2 Type II and ISO-27001 artifacts before contract extension. Can you bundle those?
[01:58] Leah (CSM): Yep, we can share our security pack. I'll include SOC 2 report redacted, ISO summary, and our SSO/KMS integration guide.
[02:10] Evan: One question on KV cache — we've seen some docs but the term was picked up weird in the automation as K V cash. How does the cache behave when you do multi-tenant dedicated nodes?
[02:22] Samir: Good call out. KV cache is per request session; in Dedicated we provide tenancy isolation so prefix caching doesn't leak across customers. There are options to pin warm cache per customer for lower cold-starts. Performance wise with quantization enabled you still see warm cache p95 reduced by roughly 30 to 50 ms depending on seq length.
[02:45] Maya: On quantization — any impact on output quality? We have some hallucination sensitivity in our rerankers.
[02:52] Samir: We recommend model-aware quant profiles. For many open models, 4-bit quantization is nearly parity for downstream rerank tasks but we can run the eval suite during the pilot to confirm.
[03:05] Jon: Let's talk numbers — what Dedicated footprint would you recommend to hit our 20M tokens/day with p95 under 300ms?
[03:12] Samir: Assuming your current prompt/response mix, we estimate a 2x footprint: ~4x the current concurrent capacity. Practically that maps to a 6 to 8 GPU Dedicated pool depending on GPU type and batching. If you want headroom for spikes, we recommend 10 GPU equivalent with burst to hosted for extreme peaks.
[03:32] Maya: And cost here — is that a monthly reserved fee?
[03:35] Alex: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly commit. We can structure a stepped ramp (6 months) where you commit to a baseline that increases after month 3. That gives a blended pricing model lower than pure on-demand.
[03:48] Priya: Does Redwood support mid-term upsizing without penalty? Our procurement prefers flexibility.
[03:53] Alex: We can add scale-up triggers in the SOW: increase capacity with 30 days notice; pricing tiers for incremental GPUs. We should capture that in the contract.
[04:03] Jon: Performance wise, can we get guarantees? p95 SLOs with remedies?
[04:08] Alex: We do SLA-backed targets for Dedicated: uptime and latency targets on the serving path. Remedies are credits — we'll need legal to finalize exact language. For pilot we'll operate without formal credit but with an escalation path.
[04:22] Maya: For the EU VPC pilot — timeline? We want to run a production-like test and validate routing and failover.
[04:30] Samir: We can provision a private pilot stack in eu-central in about 7-10 business days after we get the access and network details. The pilot run itself — we recommend a 2-hour full-load benchmark with your traces plus a 48-hour soak test if you want longer.
[04:45] Evan: What about data egress and logs — do logs leave the VPC? We need retention controls for GDPR concerns.
[04:51] Leah: We support configurable log routing; for Private we can configure logs to remain within your logging project and we can redact or disable PII in audit logs. We'll include the retention options in the security packet.
[05:03] Priya: On procurement details — we operate on net-60 PO terms. Is Redwood able to accept net-60 for enterprise deals?
[05:10] Alex: We do for enterprise contracts; we map it to our finance process in the SOW. We'll note net-60 and any early-payment discounts if relevant.
[05:18] Maya: Are there any functional gaps vs competitors we've heard about? We've run comparisons with CloudAI and Megamodel and seen similar throughput, but their EU footprint is limited. NimbusServe has a cheaper on-demand but no private VPC.
[05:32] Samir: Right — our differentiation for you is unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private plus tooling for rollout and cost-aware controls, and first-class observability. We'll show latency heatmaps in the benchmark.
[05:44] Jon: About the benchmark — Samir, can you outline the scripts and what metrics we'll get back? CPU/GPU utilization, token/sec, p50/p95, error rate, model regression?
[05:52] Samir: We'll provide a benchmark package: load generator configs, scripts to replay request traces, and a metrics dashboard that surfaces throughput, latency p50/p95/p99, GPU util, batching efficiency, and token cost estimate. We'll also run a small quality regression eval on your prompt set.
[06:10] Maya: That works. We need to coordinate a maintenance window for the 2-hour run so it doesn't hit customers during peak. We'll propose May 28 morning CET.
[06:20] Alex: Sounds good. We'll tentatively book the benchmark for May 28 and confirm in the follow-up.
[06:25] Priya: Can you also include language around audit logs and KMS in the contract? We need explicit SLAs on key rotation compatibility with our HSM.
[06:33] Leah: We'll include an appendix for KMS integrations and our supported HSM flow. If you need a direct HSM connection, that's part of the Private on-prem offering; we can scope it in the SOW.
[06:45] Evan: Quick question about fallbacks — if Dedicated is saturated, what's the fallback path?
[06:50] Samir: We support policy-based fallback: route to lower-cost model variants or to hosted pool with degraded latency but preserved availability. You control the routing policies per route.
[07:00] Jon: Ok helpful. For the extension, we were thinking of a 12-month extension with a 6-month ramp clause — is that something Redwood can do?
[07:08] Alex: Yes. We can do 12-month term with a ramp schedule and an option to convert to Private after pilot. We'll build that into the SOW. Pricing will reflect the commitment tiers.
[07:18] Priya: One more procurement thing — we need a list of subcontractors and data subprocessors for our legal team.
[07:23] Leah: I'll include a subprocessors list in the security pack.
[07:27] Maya: Great. I also want to confirm the canary and rollback tooling — if we deploy a new model and see regression, how quickly do we rollback?
[07:36] Samir: We have automated rollout policies: canary % by traffic, automatic rollback on regressions (quality gate) and metrics alerts. The platform can revert in seconds but the full KV cache warms back over minutes — we'll show that in the benchmark.
[07:50] Alex: Ok let's do a quick recap and owners. Action items are: Redwood send revised quote + SOW and security pack (Alex + Leah), provide benchmark scripts and schedule (Samir), customer to provide traces and procurement timeline (Jon + Priya).
[08:05] Priya: We'll aim to get PO window and procurement approvals by May 21.
[08:09] Jon: We'll get the request traces and prompt mix over by May 22.
[08:13] Maya: Confirming May 28 for the 2-hour benchmark morning CET, pending Evan's schedule.
[08:20] Evan: Works for me tentatively.
[08:23] Alex: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the quote. Anything else?
[08:27] Maya: No, thanks everyone.
[08:29] Alex: Thanks — talk soon.

Notes on transcript: occasional auto-transcription misfires: "SAML" transcribed on one pass as "sam el", "KV cache" as "K V cash"; speaker diarization is best effort — some short crosstalk at 05:44.

End of transcript.
